free_tier.stated: Storage and egress are whatever your VPS/host allows. No provider quota exists — the cost moves to the host's bandwidth allowance.

egress.terms: You pay the host. IPFS docs recommend putting a CDN like Cloudflare in front of the gateway and setting Cache-Control/ETag/X-Ipfs-Roots for cacheability — which is the one genuinely correct architectural move in this slot, but it is Cloudflare's free egress you are relying on, not IPFS's.

tooling: Kubo (go-ipfs), Rainbow (github.com/ipfs/rainbow), Someguy for delegated routing, Helia in-browser; rclone can talk to the Kubo RPC API via a webdav/MFS shim but there is no first-class rclone backend.
chaining: Does not multiply free storage — it only re-serves content you already paid to pin. Combined with a free pinning service it can turn 5 GB of free pinning into unmetered-looking reads, but only for 5 GB of content.
limits_note: Bandwidth of the VPS; DHT lookup latency on cold CIDs; no excess-use protection by default ('Unlike ipfs.io, a self-hosted gateway has no abuse protection by default').
reliability_note: This is the honest answer to 'does self-hosting change the economics?': it changes who meters you, not whether you are metered. It just moves the bill to the VPS or CDN.

evidence.proved: 'Put a CDN like Cloudflare in front of the IPFS gateway'; 'a self-hosted gateway has no abuse protection by default' (the vendor means it applies no excess-use protection)
'Ensure that you are correctly returning HTTP cache headers... Consider leveraging the list of CIDs in X-Ipfs-Roots'
